te: Imagine you are standing at a hospital billing counter at nine o'clock at night.
en: Imagine you are standing at a hospital billing counter at nine o'clock at night.

te: The bill is four and a half lakh rupees, and your cashless claim, where the insurance company pays the hospital directly, has just been denied.
en: The bill is four and a half lakh rupees, and your cashless claim, where the insurance company pays the hospital directly, has just been denied.

te: We told this story in our last video.
en: We told this story in our last video.

te: Here is what you need to know from it.
en: Here is what you need to know from it.

te: A cashless denial is not the end of your claim.
en: A cashless denial is not the end of your claim.

te: You can pay the hospital, and claim the money back later.
en: You can pay the hospital, and claim the money back later.

te: And if the company still says no, there is a four-step plan.
en: And if the company still says no, there is a four-step plan.

te: Collect your papers.
en: Collect your papers.

te: File for reimbursement and write to the grievance officer.
en: File for reimbursement and write to the grievance officer.

te: Register on Bima Bharosa.
en: Register on Bima Bharosa.

te: And step four, the Insurance Ombudsman.
en: And step four, the Insurance Ombudsman.

te: So you paid the bill from your pocket, collected your hospital papers, came home, and filed for reimbursement.
en: So you paid the bill from your pocket, collected your hospital papers, came home, and filed for reimbursement.

te: Three weeks later, an email lands in your inbox.
en: Three weeks later, an email lands in your inbox.

te: Either the insurance company rejects your claim all over again... or worse, out of your four and a half lakh rupee bill, they approve just one lakh twenty thousand, and cut the remaining three lakh thirty thousand rupees.
en: Either the insurance company rejects your claim all over again... or worse, out of your four and a half lakh rupee bill, they approve just one lakh twenty thousand, and cut the remaining three lakh thirty thousand rupees.

te: At that moment, many families think they only have two choices.
en: At that moment, many families think they only have two choices.

te: Choice one.
en: Choice one.

te: Hire a lawyer, go to consumer court, and wait, often for a long time, for a verdict.
en: Hire a lawyer, go to consumer court, and wait, often for a long time, for a verdict.

te: Or choice two.
en: Or choice two.

te: Answer one of those ads for a private claim recovery service, which promises to fight your case, but some ask for twenty percent or more of the money they recover as their fee.
en: Answer one of those ads for a private claim recovery service, which promises to fight your case, but some ask for twenty percent or more of the money they recover as their fee.

te: Stop right there.
en: Stop right there.

te: Before you pick either door, there is a third one.
en: Before you pick either door, there is a third one.

te: Step four of that plan.
en: Step four of that plan.

te: Today, we open that door fully, from start to finish.
en: Today, we open that door fully, from start to finish.

te: Filing a complaint costs zero rupees.
en: Filing a complaint costs zero rupees.

te: If the Ombudsman passes an award, it is binding on the insurance company.
en: If the Ombudsman passes an award, it is binding on the insurance company.

te: And if the company does not challenge the award, but pays it late, it has to pay you a penalty of five thousand rupees for every day of delay.
en: And if the company does not challenge the award, but pays it late, it has to pay you a penalty of five thousand rupees for every day of delay.
